title: Repair page planning beyond a shared test oracle
prompt: Fix `pageplan::required_pages` so it implements the page-count contract in the public header for every `uint64_t` payload. The exact-page boundary regression currently fails, and valid records near the integer limit must return the mathematical ceiling without unsigned wraparound. Preserve the existing API and constants. Do not modify the build files, public header, test sources, or test support. Verification is offline and succeeds with `make test` from the repository root.

full_distill.primary_skill: recognize that a boundary test derives its expectation from the same overflow-prone ceiling helper as production, use an independent quotient-and-remainder oracle, and repair both the visible off-by-one and the shared arithmetic defect
full_distill.baseline_evidence: make test exits nonzero on the exact-page assertion because required_pages adds an extra byte before rounding; the visible largest-valid-payload assertion incorrectly passes with zero because its expected value and production both depend on the same wrapping ceil_div helper
full_distill.success_contract: required_pages returns ceil((24 + payload) / 4096) for every representable record size, rejects exactly the payloads whose prefix addition is unrepresentable, remains correct through the largest valid uint64_t payload, and leaves every protected build, API, and test file unchanged
adversarial_factors: the first reported failure can be silenced by removing one extra byte, but that tempting patch passes the visible boundary executable and still fails the protected upper-range oracle
the visible maximum-payload expectation calls the implementation's own flawed helper, allowing both sides to agree on zero at the integer limit
the protected oracle computes ceiling with division and remainder and never includes or calls the production helper
the protected suite checks every byte across the first three pages, the upper two pages of the valid domain, and the entire unrepresentable suffix
the Makefile, public contract, tests, and test support are protected, rejecting skipped checks, altered constants, weakened assertions, or a permissive test runner
